rows.detail: Idle threshold 3 seconds; click, arrow, shortcut and tap reset enabled; AI navigation reset enabled. Tap reset is declared only on Windows/Linux.
rows.intent: Mac Karabiner outputs follow ordinary shortcut ownership per explicit manifest rationale

rows.detail: Menu calls WordReset setters; a sparse conditional canonical write must be acknowledged before the cached runtime value changes.
Configuration readers classify malformed/outdated values; setters refuse invalid types, external source changes and acquired preference scopes. Scope owners adopt and restore WordReset state.

rows.aspect: Physical four arrows and next-key context independence
rows.detail: The actual next letter and predictor receiver retain prior AI context with navigation reset off even when the word resets. Independently, navigation reset on clears the AI context when the word is retained.
Home, End, Page Up/Down, Insert and Delete reset the matcher at an unknown position even with arrow/shortcut reset disabled. Navigation reset off retains AI context.
rows.intent: Explicit manifest distinction for nonarrow navigation

rows.detail: An acknowledged Left DOWN/UP pair leaves matcher and AI context ab despite both reset settings being enabled; the next c feeds abc.
With arrow reset off and tap reset on the word wrongly resets; with the inverse settings it wrongly remains. The actual catalogue allows arrow_left and the native event pair is acknowledged.
A held tap-hold Ctrl+S reports tap_hold=true and follows tap reset off even while ordinary shortcut reset is enabled.

rows.aspect: Direct undo/redo chords and AI unknown-edit clearing
rows.detail: Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z forget unknown-edit AI context regardless of navigation reset off. The word deliberately remains when shortcut reset is disabled.
rows.intent: Explicit Main unknown-edit policy independent of word setting

rows.detail: Ctrl+V clears unknown-edit AI context; Ctrl+S preserves it with navigation reset off. No actual clipboard operation runs.
Terminal Alt+B clears AI context with navigation reset off; the same GUI chord retains it. Main explicitly applies a conservative rule to selected Readline chords.
The generic tap-navigation policy retains AI context with navigation reset off, unlike direct Ctrl+V. The action receiver records dispatch; clipboard data is not pasted.
rows.intent: Source explicitly classifies all tap commands as navigation; no extra confirmed finding

rows.detail: A long idle before Backspace does not wipe the preceding word. Typing ab, Backspace and c produces ac in both matcher and context.

Ctrl+Backspace establishes a word start and clears AI context. Alt+Backspace establishes an unknown start and clears it. Super follows the same source branch; native application bindings were not measured.

rows.aspect: Known empty line after SelectAll/browser address chord
rows.detail: Ctrl+A in an editor and Ctrl+L in a browser preserve known empty-line authority through Backspace. Terminal Ctrl+A lacks that authority and the boundary becomes unknown.
rows.intent: Source logical whole-field contracts; actual selected-range receipt unmeasured

rows.detail: After the three-second threshold, an ordinary c forgets the old word and AI context. Zero disables idle reset; registered cases cover shared resolution and bounds.
Escape establishes a word start. With navigation reset off the AI context retains ab and the next c produces abc.

rows.aspect: Bare Enter GUI versus terminal and control Enter
rows.detail: GUI typed newline retains ab\nc even with navigation reset enabled. A terminal resets the word to its prompt and clears AI context only with navigation reset on. Ctrl+Enter uses the control route.
rows.intent: Typed multiline versus control/navigation policy; no universal Enter reset obligation inferred

rows.detail: Shift+Enter uses the bare typed-newline route and terminal prompt reset. This modifier limitation is already documented in routed memory.
rows.intent: Known limitation, not asserted deliberate behavior

rows.aspect: Pointer privacy reset with navigation retention
rows.detail: A click invalidates field authority and clears AI context before the navigation reset, so disabling navigation reset does not preserve that text. Click word reset off establishes an unknown boundary.
rows.intent: Privacy owner supersedes navigation preference; preserve this guard

rows.detail: Raw Tab and a changed field invalidate and clear old context. This does not certify input reception by a native successor field.
The actual Main pause-reset callback clears both buffers; disabled AI retains nothing. The runtime pause controller and native desktop resume are outside this role's execution.

rows.status: guarded boundary with missing semantic publication
rows.basis: actual Writer/Broker plus source device policy
rows.detail: The actual Writer acknowledgments are recorded; source policy excludes the own uinput device. Feeding synthetic output back into the matcher is not a valid repair for the missing owned notification.
Public action dispatch executes. Physical touchpad acquisition, native caret/text/selection, IME, a model request, runtime latency and heap behavior were not measured.
